about: The dimensions tools/parity.py checks (docs/PARITY.md). A check is one Go test whose expected values are Slack's own output: Slack's JavaScript run in node, or answers and messages captured from live Slack. Tests whose expected values someone wrote by hand from reading Slack's code are rules, and they don't go here. A check with a "snapshot" reads Slack's values from that file (its "slack" block says where they came from, and --refresh can capture them again); the others keep them in the test and say where they came from in "oracle". The areas list every part of Slack's client Clack implements, so the report can name the ones no check covers.

areas.name: Composer: the ":" emoji list
areas.gaps: Ranking only, for a few queries. Skin tones, the list's drawing and keyboard handling are not compared with Slack's output.

areas.name: Composer: the "@", "#" and "/" lists
areas.gaps: Only the fuzzy matcher's similarity is differential. The ranking of people, channels, usergroups and commands is tested against rules (TestAutocompleteSlackPeople, TestAutocompleteSlackChannels, TestAutocompleteSlackCommandsAndEmoji), not against Slack's output.

areas.name: Composer: formatting and markdown
areas.gaps: Only Mod+Shift+F (convertMarkdown) is differential. Markdown applied while typing and the formatting bar are tested against rules.

areas.name: Composer: link and message slugs
areas.gaps: The elements' shapes only. Slack's server computes a link slug's display_url, so Clack has nothing of its own to compare there; fakeslack's copy of it is checked as a fake-server check.

areas.name: Composer: sending, editing, drafts and scheduling
Messages: rich text, Block Kit, attachments and unfurls
Files and snippet previews
areas.gaps: Only the snippet HTML cut (html-truncate) is differential. The inline video player's rules (fileIsPlayableVideo, the pill's time, the mute and volume prefs) are read from Slack's code; no check compares them with Slack's output.

areas.name: Threads
areas.gaps: A link or pill without thread_ts into an AI app's DM opens the DM at the message; Slack's jumpViaRoutes (wc0P) opens it as a thread in the main window, or the app's chat tab, when AI apps are on and the app is valid (OePe K, Db4L wP, 3NYU yk). Clack doesn't model AI-app DMs yet.

areas.name: Home, DMs, Later and the other views
Invite people
areas.gaps: Splitting and tokenizing the typed addresses only. The modal's sends and answers are tested against rules.

areas.name: Themes and colours
areas.gaps: Only the custom-colour palettes (HCT) are differential.

areas.name: Desktop notifications
areas.gaps: The macOS options and the Windows text cut and ids. The Windows toast's layout differs from Slack's on purpose (see the deliberate differences).

areas.name: Desktop window placement
areas.gaps: Default and reopened bounds and the fit on a display only.

areas.name: Emoji rendering and the emoji picker

deliberate.slack: Slack desktop's toastXml (EH.createToastNotification, 4.53.276 win32) has a header, a reply box and line limits, and titles a message toast with the channel's name.
deliberate.clack: Clack's toast is Chrome's (Chromium's notification_template_builder.cc): the title as the webapp wrote it ("New message in #general"), the body, the workspace, Clack's icon, the time.

deliberate.what: A slack://channel link whose thread_ts names a reply
deliberate.slack: handleParsedDeepLink (boot-render VxbD) sends slack://channel?id=C&thread_ts=<reply> to jumpToMessage, which opens toThread keyed on the reply; ThreadView (eTbq) takes the reply as rootMsg (getMessage(ch, threadTs)) and requestReplies (client-boot 0VEE) keeps what conversations.replies answers for that ts, the whole thread parent first. So Slack (build 2c0d02ca130f) draws a broken pane: the reply as the root, the parent and its siblings under it.
deliberate.clack: A logged guard opens the reply's thread at the reply instead, its root highlighted in the conversation: jumpViaRoutes for a reply core holds (ui: jumpToMessage: its thread_ts … is a reply in …), OpenThread's guard for a route naming one (ui: thread open: …), the pane's hand-over once conversations.replies says so (ui: thread pane: its root … is a reply in …). It never stands in for fixing a caller that builds a reply-rooted route: Clack's own routes take the reply's thread first, as Slack's do.
deliberate.decided: thread-open-root's parity review, 2026-11-18 (kept as a logged guard, recorded here with this evidence)

elsewhere.what: TestIconsMatchSlack and TestArtMatchesSlack: Clack's icons and illustrations against the glyphs of Slack's icon font and its SVG art, by ink, with pass/fail thresholds.
TestTextMatchesChrome and TestTextInk: Clack's text against Chrome's in the same font, with thresholds, plus text_render_compare.py's side-by-sides.
sidebar_rows_ref.py and rail_ref.py: the sidebar's rows and the rail next to Slack's markup under Slack's shipping CSS, measured. Pass/fail only with SIDEBAR_ROWS_STRICT.
compact_ref.py: channel and thread rows, Clean and Compact, next to Slack's markup under Slack's CSS; it fails when a row height is off by more than 1px.
activity_ref.py: Activity rows next to Slack's markup under Slack's CSS. Side-by-sides, no pass/fail.
threads_ref.py: the thread pane's states in Slack's markup under Slack's CSS. Side-by-sides, no pass/fail.
emoji_render_compare.py: Clack's standard emoji against Chrome's, cell by cell. No pass/fail.
